everett1825.summary: Everett's private portrait of Francisco Zea Bermúdez, the Spanish minister whom he calls the prime Minister, and his reading of the refusal to recognise the new American states. Zea's frankness is real or assumed, and he said things he could not believe himself; he came into the cabinet through Ugarte, a creature of Russia, then sent him off on a mission to Turin; he is able, hard-working, liberal in conversation, less Spanish in manner than any Spaniard Everett has met. The foreign ministers think him privately well disposed to recognition but unable to risk his place against his rivals; the influence of the Emperor Alexander is against it, from a spirit of opposition to England rather than a regard for legitimacy.
everett1825.en:
The reading of record since 24 Nov 2026. It is the text that the State Department code sheet (NARA M97 roll 13
frames 1056-1057; keywe028everett1825.tsv) gives for the groups of everett1825collatedtranscription.txt,
group by group in everett1825collateddecryption.txt, joined into words. English, so no translation.

The words are those of the three earlier readings: WAINUT's passages A, B and C (everett1825reading.md), Brice
Dudout's eight pages (dudout/texts/), both made with the table rebuilt in ../jqa, and the State Department's
decipherment of the time (beling/perioddecipherment.txt). This file marks, against the code sheet, which
words the key gives and which it does not. It supplies two words of its own, th[at] and [under] on MS p. 5, where
the earlier readings left the passage open; both are bracketed.
